title: Forms and input usability
goal: Make a form usable and test keyboard workflows without replacing data rules with UI.
prerequisites: 1c-enterprise.a 4; A1–A2: separate infobase, catalogs, references and documents; synthetic data only.
outcomes: Make a form usable and test keyboard workflows without replacing data rules with UI.
Complete valid input using the keyboard.
Enter−1 and correct only the duration.
sections: Place customer, service and duration in input order. Labels must state units; required fields should be identifiable without color alone. Save must communicate its outcome. A starter form does not need dozens of buttons: tie every action to an operator task and a verifiable state.

Start assembly with one complete operator route:select customer/service, enter duration, save and find the request again. Add report variants andUIimprovements afterwards. This ties objects to actions and exposes missing references or fields early, rather than accumulating disconnected screens. Every object should support a named workflow and a measurable persistence check.
A form element differs from a data attribute

An input displays an attribute but does not itself create persistent storage. An unbound control can lose entered values. Trace control→formattribute→object. Relabeling must preserve links to stored data. Appearance is not a substitute for choosing the business data type.

Catalogs represent reusable entities; documents represent individual requests. One customer can have many requests and one service many customers. Test that multiplicity synthetically. Creating a new equal-named customer for every request breaks the model even when totals match. Check catalog counts and reference identity separately from arithmetic and appearance.

For negative minutes, name the field and allowed range while preserving other inputs. Do not clear the form or create a new document just to retry. A keyboard user must locate the error and return to Save. A rejected command must not show a false success message.

Usable forms do not replace write rules. Invalid minutes must reject through alternative input routes, and correcting one field must preserve other input. After rejection, perform a valid operation, close and reopen the document. This verifies bothUIutility and durable state rather than merely the ability to display an error.

Use Tab, select a reference, enter duration, save and reopen without a mouse. Check a long service name and narrow window. A responsive Nexus page does not prove the 1C desktop client works on a phone: record the actual client and device. Screenshots supplement the workflow protocol rather than replacing execution.

A complete teaching system explains each reported number through source documents and an independent small-data sum. Change one document in a fresh copy and verify recalculation, then reread the source to prove independence. Bind changes and snapshots to work IDs. Matching an infobase name never authorizes overwriting a prior submission.

lab.environment: Official 1C 8.3.27.x, new training-service-desk copy. Command labels depend on the configuration interface; verify outcomes against data. Training-edition limits are explicit.
steps: Create a separate work copy; record its ID, source ID and platform/configuration build. Never restore over your source.

Reopen the copy, repeat the checks and reconcile the unchanged source. Preserve failures separately from the corrected attempt.
expected: Fields have a logical focus order; writing is confirmed by rereading.
Other fields remain; success appears only after a write.

mistakes: Treat an expected value as an observed execution.
Reconcile the result in the specified environment and attach the protocol; the browser model does not execute BSL.
Modify the source infobase while experimenting.
Work on a new copy and verify the source by reopening it separately.

quiz.question: Does an unbound form control guarantee persistence?
quiz.explanation: It needs model binding and reread verification.
